segments.caption: Meet Capy: a team of AI capybaras that babysits your GPU training runs, so you can sleep.

segments.html:
Agents say “done” when they aren't.

Real run from our test benchmark · single agent · Nemotron 3.5 Super · same tools as Capy

Single agent

  1. checked 50 steps: 101.5% of baseline
  2. noticed the checkpoint config change, called it transient
  3. declared: “self-recovered… No persistent root cause identified.”

What actually happened

  1. config v43 moved checkpoints to a slow archive tier: every 100 steps the job froze for 2+ minutes
  2. a 50-step window can miss every freeze
  3. throughput stayed at 78%: ~114 GPU-hours lost every hour
segments.say: A single AI agent got a slow training run on five hundred twelve GPUs. It checked fifty steps, saw a hundred and one percent, and declared it self-recovered. It was still twenty-two percent slow.
segments.caption: A single agent checked 50 steps, saw 101%, and declared “self-recovered”. The run was still 22% slow.

segments.say: Same incident, Capy's turn. Every GPU looks healthy, and no prompt describes this fault.
segments.caption: Same incident, Capy's turn. Every GPU looks healthy, and no prompt describes this fault.

segments.say: First, Capy writes the definition of done: two hundred steps at ninety-seven percent, a proven cause, and a skeptic who agrees. Fifty lucky steps can't pass.
segments.caption: First, the definition of done: 200 steps at ≥97%, a cause that explains ≥90%, and a skeptic who agrees.

segments.say: Four field capys on Nemotron Nano sweep GPUs, network, storage and changes in parallel.
segments.caption: Four Nemotron 3 Nano field capys sweep GPUs, network, storage and changes in parallel.

segments.say: Detective Capy, on Nemotron Super, spots the contradiction: steps are normal, throughput isn't. A config change moved checkpoints to a slow tier, so every hundred steps the job freezes for over two minutes.
segments.caption: Nemotron 3.5 Super: steps are normal, throughput isn't. Checkpoint saves went from 4 s to 140 s after a config change.

segments.say: A counterfactual on the step timings proves it explains ninety-five percent of the slowdown.
segments.caption: Proof gate: removing the slow saves explains 95% of the slowdown.

segments.say: Inspector Doubt, on Qwen three point eight so its blind spots differ, tries to break the theory, and upholds it.
segments.caption: Inspector Doubt (Qwen 3.8, a different model family) tries to falsify it, and upholds.

segments.say: The fix needs a restart, so Capy pings you once, with the proof and the cost attached. One tap, back to sleep.
segments.caption: A restart is disruptive, so Capy pings you once, with the proof and the cost attached.

segments.say: It then measures two hundred real steps across two checkpoints.
segments.caption: Verification: 200 real steps across two checkpoints. Saves are back to 4 s.

segments.say: Verified at one hundred percent. Case closed: one ping, seven cents of inference.
segments.caption: Verified at 100%. Case closed: one ping, 7 cents of inference on Crusoe Managed Inference.

segments.say: On thirty-four unseen incidents, both agents fixed ninety-seven percent. The difference is trust: the single agent falsely declared done once, and drained a healthy node once. Capy did neither, and when it couldn't prove a cause, it escalated instead of guessing.
segments.caption: Both fixed 97% of 34 unseen incidents. Single agent: 1 false “done”, 1 wasted drain. Capy: 0 and 0, and it escalated the one it couldn't prove.
